title: Optimize Toolkit playbook: micro-interactions, accessibility-ready screenshots for batching/caching & quant UI
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact playbook and a set of production-ready visual assets that demonstrate Optimize Toolkit recommendations for batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles. Deliverables should include annotated screenshots for docs, interactive micro-interaction prototypes (GIFs) for the console onboarding tour, accessibility-ready alt text and keyboard flows, and 3 size variants for marketing screenshots. The goal is to reduce time-to-action for engineering teams by giving clear, scannable advice and examples that can be inserted into quickstarts and in-console guidance. Work must align with Console design tokens and not add new color/spacing tokens. Include guidance copy for trade-offs (latency vs cost vs quality) and an example prompt set used to generate the example outputs.
micro_interactions: Quant selector hover + tooltip with brief quality/cost summary (300ms loop GIF)
Batching slider live preview: sample latency estimate animating as slider moves (500ms GIF)
KV cache toggle animation showing prefix cache hit visualization (400ms GIF)
Onboarding card entrance and quick-accept CTA microcopy (250ms)
accessibility_notes: All screenshots must include alt-text snippets (provided in assets) and short captions for non-sighted users.
Ensure color contrast for token meter and quant badges meets WCAG AA at small sizes.
Keyboard-only flows: quant selector and batching slider must be operable via arrow keys and have clear focus outlines in the prototype.
Provide screen-reader phrasing for dynamic changes (e.g., 'Estimated latency: 120ms; estimated cost per 1k tokens: $0.02').
review_feedback: PM Marco Hernandez: prefer a compact card variant for early users; emphasize a single recommended profile with 'Why this?' microcopy.
Eng lead Priya Rao: confirm that token-meter values match the runtime telemetry output (ENG-4120) before finalizing numbers.
Research Samir Gupta: run quick hallway test with 5 engineers to validate that screenshots reduce follow-up questions about 'when to quantize'.
Legal: add brief note about model quality variance at high quant levels (draft provided in docs link).
